rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open-source HM Land Registry dataset created for INSPIRE compliance.
INSPIRE contains locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry's wider freehold Index Polygons database.
INSPIRE is divided into separate local-authority files and a boundary polygon can appear in two authority files.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
HM Land Registry directs users to Find a Property with the INSPIRE ID to obtain title registration and plan information.
INSPIRE polygons show position and indicative extent, not the definitive legal extent of a registered title.
The individual title plan is required to identify the registered-title extent.
One title number can contain several separate polygons and each polygon has a separate INSPIRE ID.
Missing INSPIRE ID can indicate unregistered land, leasehold registration or another excluded tenure.
Business e-services MapSearch exposes the full Index Polygon dataset but requires the relevant customer service context and is not the anonymous public INSPIRE download.
INSPIRE data and attributes are reusable under the Open Government Licence.
INSPIRE reuse requires HM Land Registry attribution.
Reuse of INSPIRE polygon geometry also requires Ordnance Survey attribution.
INSPIRE updates on the first Sunday of each month and represents data from the previous month.
The current download index states publication on 5 July 2026 and lists both Barnet and Enfield.
HM Land Registry publishes the public INSPIRE authority files as GML.
The National Polygon Service is a separate licensed chargeable service containing National Polygon, Title Descriptor and Title Number/UPRN Look Up datasets.
National Polygon includes freehold and leasehold titles, while public INSPIRE is a freehold-focused subset.
A paid National Polygon source must not be silently substituted for the anonymous public INSPIRE source when validating the free-source workflow.
Planning Data publishes a dedicated title-boundary dataset described as Land Registry Index polygons showing position and indicative extent of registered property.
The title-boundary dataset page currently reports 2,595,903 title-boundary entities.
The title-boundary dataset page reports one data provider.
The title-boundary collector last ran on 26 November 2025.
The title-boundary page says new data was last found on 26 November 2025.
The dataset origin notice says some data was created by MHCLG and is being replaced with authoritative sources.
The title-boundary dataset is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
The title-boundary attribution identifies HM Land Registry copyright and database rights 2026.
The title-boundary attribution also identifies Ordnance Survey copyright and database rights 2026 for polygon geometry.
Title-boundary entities use the dataset and prefix value title-boundary.
Indexed title-boundary entity pages identify HM Land Registry as the organisation.
Title-boundary entity pages expose multipolygon geometry.
Title-boundary entity pages also expose a representative point.
Title-boundary entity pages expose start-date, end-date and entry-date fields.
Title-boundary entity pages expose a quality field which may be blank or authoritative depending on the record.
The title-boundary reference value is distinct from the Planning Data numeric entity identifier.
Current Planning Data API docs allow coordinate queries to target a named dataset using latitude and longitude.
The documented coordinate query returns entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
Planning Data documents UPRN search through q as more precise than coordinate search for registered properties.
Dataset-level counts and indexed examples cannot bind any of the three real candidates without an exact candidate query response, so candidate promotion remains fail closed.
The Environment Agency exposes a public ArcGIS FeatureServer named LIDAR_Tiles_Catalogues in British National Grid EPSG:27700.
The FeatureServer contains a LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents layer with layer ID 0.
The DTM Time Stamped layer is a polygon feature layer describing the extent of individual terrain surveys.
The DTM layer supports JSON, GeoJSON and PBF query formats.
The DTM layer reports a maximum record count of 2000.
The DTM Time Stamped layer exposes a filename attribute.
The layer exposes an os_ref attribute for OS-grid referencing.
The layer exposes sd_flown and ed_flown survey-date attributes.
The layer exposes pt_count and pt_spacing attributes describing source point-cloud sampling.
The layer exposes transform and geoid attributes for transformation provenance.
The layer exposes a filepath attribute that can identify the source file path.
The layer exposes a year attribute and a supplied-date attribute.
The layer exposes a latest attribute for source/version context.
The layer exposes a polygon_id attribute for survey-feature identity.
The Time Stamped DTM archive provides terrain rasters at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions depending on survey.
Time Stamped DTM data is supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files.
Time Stamped DTM elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
The Time Stamped dataset record states quarterly update frequency and a survey period extending to 18 April 2024.
The current DTM 1m composite remains a separate 2022 composite product covering about 99 percent of England at 1m resolution.
The DTM layer schema provides a stronger official route for exact survey provenance, but no TQ2892-filtered feature or candidate numeric elevation is promoted until its query response is read back.
The OS Downloads API technical specification states that OpenData endpoints do not require an API key.
The Downloads API is intended to automate discovery and retrieval of OS OpenData products.
The OpenData download endpoint uses the path /products/{productId}/downloads.
productId is a required path parameter for an OpenData download request.
fileName is an optional OpenData download filter.
format is an optional OpenData download filter.
subformat is an optional OpenData download filter.
area is an optional geographical filter for OpenData downloads.
TQ is an explicitly documented allowed area value for the area filter.
When redirect is supplied and exactly one download matches, the API returns HTTP 307 to the actual download location.
A normal successful OpenData download-list request returns HTTP 200 with JSON file information.
An unknown OpenData request can return HTTP 404 with a human-readable message.
OS states that API content may change as products are changed, added or removed and recommends discovery methods for the most current content.
The Downloads API exposes OpenData product metadata as well as download links.
Current OS Terrain 50 documentation describes an annually updated July OpenData terrain product.
Terrain 50 uses 10km tiles and 50m grid spacing.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid rows contain 200 pixel values ordered west to east.
Terrain 50 grid heights are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre and are interpreted at pixel centres.
Terrain 50 metadata uses British National Grid horizontally and Ordnance Datum Newlyn vertically.
Live official Terrain50 product JSON and TQ29 download bytes still require direct readback before the two candidate grid cells can be promoted.

blocked_gates.rule: The July 2026 HMLR index and INSPIRE semantics are readable, but exact Barnet/Enfield GML href, bytes and SHA remain unavailable because the download page still enters a redirect loop in this execution environment.
Exact HMLR INSPIRE IDs and native-BNG containment for all three real candidates remain unresolved; paid National Polygon is not substituted for the free public INSPIRE source.
Planning Data now exposes a public title-boundary dataset and exact coordinate-query contract, but exact parameterised responses for the three candidate points remain blocked by execution URL safety.
Exact Planning Data title-boundary binding for parcel refs 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remains absent.
The official DTM Time Stamped FeatureServer layer and provenance fields are readable, but a candidate/TQ2892-filtered feature response has not yet been read back.
Exact candidate WCS or GeoTIFF bytes, SHA, NoData interpretation and numeric elevations remain absent.
Official Downloads API semantics and the TQ area filter are verified, but live Terrain50 product JSON and TQ download-list responses have not been read back.
OS Terrain50 TQ29 download bytes, SHA and row149 col173/174 numeric height values remain absent.
F-host recovery plus HD2 015 and HD1 016/025/identity-provenance runtime outputs remain absent.
